Notifications

notifyd is the desk's notification service. Anything on the Bus can post a notification: an app saying a job is done, or an agent asking "is this okay?" with Yes and No buttons. The desk shows it as a toast in the top right corner and lists it on the Notifications page of the right-hand panel. When the human presses a button, closes it, or lets it time out, notifyd records that outcome and publishes it, so the sender finds out without anyone switching to a dedicated app.

One notifyd runs per desk session (notifyd@N), under the Bus name notify.

Posting a notification

send notify notify.send body='{"summary":"Build finished","source":"cbc"}'

The reply comes back at once with the new notification's id: {"id": 7, "status": "open"}. Nothing waits for the human.

To ask a question, add up to four buttons, and optionally a timeout:

send notify notify.send body='{"summary":"Deploy to staging?","actions":[{"id":"yes","label":"Yes"},{"id":"no","label":"No"}],"timeout_ms":300000}'

Hearing the answer

Every change is published on the topic notify.changed. The inner command says what happened, and the body is the notification as notify.get shows it:

Inner commandWhen
notification.createda notification was posted
notification.answeredthe human pressed a button; outcome.action is its id
notification.closedany other outcome: dismissed, expired or closed

Subscribe before you send, so the answer cannot arrive before you are listening, and match on the id the send returned. If you were disconnected, notify.get {id} tells you the outcome afterwards.

An expired question was not answered. Treat it as "no answer", never as yes.

Verbs

VerbBodyReply
notify.sendsummary, and optionally body, app, source, actions ([{id, label}]), timeout_ms, request_id, thread{id, status}
notify.get{id}the notification, with outcome once it has one
notify.list{all?}open notifications, oldest first; all: true includes answered ones
notify.action{id, action}the human pressed a button (the toast calls this)
notify.dismiss{id}the human closed it without choosing
notify.close{id}the sender, or the Notifications page, withdrew it
notify.close_all{}closes every open notification without buttons; questions stay

Each notification gets exactly one outcome. The first one wins, and a later button press or timeout is refused with ALREADY_ANSWERED.

notify.action, notify.dismiss and notify.close_all are the human's own acts, made through the desk's scenes, so notifyd takes them only from callers on this node (the broker's broker_origin stamp). A peer across the mesh can post and read notifications but never answer one for the person. That matters for questions such as portald's screen-share consent.

Errors come back as {error_code, message}: rc 10 USAGE (a bad body), rc 13 FORBIDDEN (not a local caller), rc 14 NOT_FOUND, rc 15 ALREADY_ANSWERED, rc 16 TOO_MANY_OPEN.

Limits

A summary is at most 120 characters, a body 500, and a button label 32. A notification has at most four buttons. At most eight questions can wait for an answer at once; the ninth is refused until one is answered. notifyd keeps the last 200 notifications, and never drops one that is still open.

State

Notifications are kept in one JSON file, rewritten atomically on every change: ~/.local/state/mixos/notifyd/state.json, or $MIXOS_NOTIFYD_STATE. After a restart, open notifications stay open and their timeouts carry on; notifyd never answers on the human's behalf. A state file it cannot read is moved aside, never overwritten.
